messages:
sam: Heads-up — after the RBAC change we rolled last night, a handful of users in the Sales groups lost access to the Dedicated cluster. SCIM still shows the groups but members are empty for several orgs. Also seeing KMS decrypt failures in the scim-provisioner logs. Can someone help triage? :rotating_light:
jordan: Paging in ops. Can you paste the scim-provisioner pod logs and the exact RBAC diff you applied?
maya: I have the diff, applied at 02:14 UTC. It removed the old `sales_readonly` binding and added `project:read` with a new group matcher. Attaching snippet: ```diff
- roleBinding: sales_readonly -> group:sales_*
+ roleBinding: project:read -> group:realm_sales_v2
```
leila: Two potential failures: 1) SCIM mapping mismatch (group rename) leaving users unbound, 2) KMS keys used to decrypt SCIM tokens rotated and not rewrapped for the provisioner. Which logs do we have?
sam: Paste of relevant lines from scim-provisioner logs: ```
2026-03-20T02:26:03Z ERROR scim-provisioner: failed to decrypt token: KMSClientError: InvalidCiphertextException
2026-03-20T02:26:03Z WARN scim-provisioner: skipping user sync for group realm_sales_v2
2026-03-20T02:27:45Z INFO scim-provisioner: received SCIM job for group sales@acme-co
2026-03-20T02:27:45Z ERROR scim-provisioner: map error: attribute 'members' returned empty set
```
jordan: That InvalidCiphertextException screams wrong key ARN or key policy blocking decrypt. Any recent KMS key rotation?
maya: We rotated the workspace KMS master key last week as part of a routine key rotation but didn't rewrap some long-lived tokens. I flagged that as low risk because most services re-wrapped OK. Looks like scim-provisioner is one of the holdouts.
leila: Okay. Two parallel actions: A) quick mitigation so users regain access; B) remediation plan. Mitigation ideas: temporarily rebind an emergency RBAC override to restore access, AND run a one-off SCIM bulk sync using a new token we create locally (so we don't need provenance until we fix key policies). Thoughts?
sam: Emergency override sounds safest short-term. Jordan — can you create a short-lived cluster-admin role binding for affected groups/orgs? I'll open the incident channel and notify customer-facing teams.
jordan: On it, creating a timeboxed binding for 4 hours. Command I'm running: ```kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: emergency-sales-override
  namespace: redwood-dedicated-sales
subjects:
- kind: Group
  name: realm_sales_v2
roleRef:
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: dedicated-cluster-read
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
EOF
```
ops-bot: Action logged: temporary_role_binding created by jordan at 2026-03-20T02:33:12Z (expires 4h)
leila: For remediation we need to: 1) rewrap SCIM tokens with the new KMS key, 2) add unit checks in the rollout to validate SCIM-member lists before RBAC switchover, 3) audit KMS key policies to ensure principal scim-provisioner has decrypt permissions.
maya: I can rewrap tokens — but we need KMS permissions. Who owns the KMS key policy?
sam: Security owns the policy. @leila can you add the service principal `scim-provisioner@infra.redwood` to decrypt on the key? Also add a short TTL rewrap script in the deploy pipeline.
leila: Will do. Quick check of audit logs in Console shows SCIM webhook calls arriving from the IdP and our internal agent, but the user->group mapping failed after the rename. Audit entry example: ```
{"ts":"2026-03-20T02:27:45Z","actor":"okta:acme-admin","event":"scim.group.update","details":"groupRealm=realm_sales_v2,members=0"}
```
jordan: Interesting — the IdP (Okta) still uses `sales@acme-co` as primary group name; our SCIM transform expects `realm_sales_v2`. So two problems: token decryption AND mapping mismatch for group rename. That explains members empty.
maya: I can run a targeted bulk import to map `sales@acme-co` -> `realm_sales_v2` if we create a rewrapped token.
sam: Go for it. Also, Leila, please run a KMS policy audit and post the diff. We need to update runbooks: do not rotate KMS master keys without a pre-check for long-lived encrypted assets (SCIM tokens, SSO session store).
leila: Uploading current and proposed key policy diffs now. Key change required adding `arn:aws:iam::redwood:role/scim-provisioner` to `kms:Decrypt`. I pushed the change, waiting for AWS propagation.
ops-bot: KMS policy updated by leila at 2026-03-20T02:44:01Z. Propagation OK.
idp-bot: SCIM token rewrap attempt result: success for token id tok-4821, failed for tok-4790 (expired).
maya: Re-run the bulk sync with rewrapped token tok-4821: ```curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer tok-4821" https://scim.internal.redwood/v2/BulkSync -d '{"map": [{"from":"sales@acme-co","to":"realm_sales_v2"}]}'```
ops-bot: Bulk sync job queued: job_id=bulk-20260320-01, estimated 45s
ops-bot: Bulk sync job completed: job_id=bulk-20260320-01, created 312 user->group bindings
leila: Confirmed in audit: members count for realm_sales_v2 now 312. RBAC checks show access restored for most affected users.
sam: Nice. Please capture timeline for postmortem: root cause = KMS rotation + incomplete rewrap of long-lived tokens, exacerbated by group rename and lack of SCIM pre-checks during RBAC rollout.
jordan: Action items I tracked: - revert any other RBAC renames until we have a test harness - add pre-deploy CI that runs a SCIM dry-run - add alert when SCIM member counts drop >20% after group change
maya: I'll follow up with a patch to the deploy pipeline to rewrap tokens automatically during KMS rotate, and a migration script to auto-map old group names (with a flag).
leila: Security actions: update KMS runbook, rotate any expired tokens (tok-4790), and add monitoring on InvalidCiphertextException spikes. Also, we'll include a sign-off checkpoint for any RBAC changes touching production groups.
sam: Thanks team. I'm opening an incident postmortem doc and assigning owners per the list. We'll notify customers impacted and offer remediation notes. If anyone sees residual 403s after 03:10 UTC, ping here. :thumbsup:
